tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Stanislavski and Naturalism

questions.question: Explain how an actor would use Stanislavski's 'magic if' and 'given circumstances' to prepare for a role.
questions.correctAnswer: Given circumstances provide the factual foundation; magic if personalises the situation. An actor first researches all the facts, then asks 'what would I do?' to find truthful responses. Give a specific character example.

questions.question: What is subtext and why is it important in naturalistic performance? Give an example.
questions.correctAnswer: Subtext is the unspoken meaning beneath dialogue. In naturalism, characters don't say what they mean — the actor must play the subtext, not just the lines. E.g. 'I'm fine' said with tears = subtext of pain.

questions.question: Compare Stanislavski's approach to Brecht's — how do they differ in their relationship with the audience?
questions.correctAnswer: Stanislavski wants the audience to empathise and believe (emotional identification); Brecht wants the audience to think critically (alienation effect). Stanislavski hides the art; Brecht makes the audience aware they are watching theatre.
